_note: 책 QR 보너스 연습 — 안티 작성 · Claude 검토

cards.en: The sky is clear. (subject with final consonant)
The train passes by. (subject without final consonant)
Your voice is nice. (voice is the subject of adjective)
I have a question. (subject of existence 있다)
I do not have time. (subject of non-existence 없다)
Who came? (누구 + 가 = 누가)
I will do it. (저 + 가 = 제가)
He became a doctor. (complement/subject of 되다)

quiz.q: Which sentence correctly uses the subject marker 이/가?
quiz.why: 가방 ends with a final consonant (ㅇ), so it takes 이 instead of 가. 무겁다 is an adjective, so it takes the subject marker 이.

quiz.q: Which form is correct when attaching the subject marker 가 to 저 (I, humble)?
quiz.why: When attaching the subject marker 가 to the first-person pronoun 저, it changes to 제가.

quiz.q: Which sentence has an INCORRECT particle?
quiz.why: 우산 ends with the final consonant ㄴ, so it must take 이 (우산이 없어요), not 가.

quiz.q: Fill in the blank: '누가 커피를 마셔요? - 민호___ 마셔요.'
quiz.why: 민호 ends with a vowel (호), so the subject marker 가 is attached to answer who performs the action.

quiz.q: Which particle fits in: '한국어 공부___ 재미있어요.'?
quiz.why: 공부 ends in a vowel, and 재미있다 (to be fun) is an adjective taking the subject marker 가.

fill.q: 밖에 조용히 봄비___ 내려요.
fill.en: Spring rain falls quietly outside.

fill.q: 창밖 풍경___ 참 아름다워요.
fill.en: The view outside the window is truly beautiful.

fill.q: 어디___ 아파요?
fill.en: Where hurts?

fill.q: 오늘 저녁에 시간___ 있어요?
fill.en: Do you have time this evening?

fill.q: 누가 먼저 발표해요? - 제___ 할게요.
fill.en: Who presents first? I will do it.

cards.en: As for me, I am an American. (topic without final consonant)
The teacher is kind. (topic with final consonant)
Today, I am busy. (marking time as the topic)
My older brother is tall. (topic in double subject construction)
The movie is interesting. (movie as the topic)
I like apples, but I do not like pears. (contrast)
I drink coffee (though perhaps not other drinks). (focus/contrast)
To Korea, I have been. (combining with 에 for contrast)

quiz.q: Which sentence correctly attaches 은/는 to a word with a final consonant?
quiz.why: 동생 ends with a final consonant (ㅇ), so it takes 은 instead of 는.

quiz.q: What nuance does the particle 는 convey in '여름은 덥지만 겨울은 추워요'?
quiz.why: The particle 은/는 is frequently used to highlight contrast between two opposing subjects or topics.

quiz.q: Which sentence has an INCORRECT particle?
quiz.why: 도서관 ends with a final consonant (ㄴ), so it must take 은 (도서관은 조용해요), not 는.

quiz.q: Fill in the blank: '지민 씨___ 어디에 살아요?'
quiz.why: 씨 ends with a vowel, so the topic marker 는 attaches to form the topic of the question.

quiz.q: Which sentence best expresses: 'I do not drink alcohol, but I do drink water'?
quiz.why: Using 은/는 on both nouns emphasizes the contrast between alcohol (not drinking) and water (drinking).

fill.q: 저___ 한국에서 대학교에 다녀요.
fill.en: As for me, I attend university in Korea.

fill.q: 이 책___ 아주 흥미진진해요.
fill.en: As for this book, it is very intriguing.

fill.q: 형은 운동을 잘하지만 동생___ 공부를 잘해요.
fill.en: My older brother is good at sports, but my younger sibling is good at studying.

fill.q: 지금___ 회의 중이라 통화하기 어려워요.
fill.en: Right now, I am in a meeting, so it is hard to speak on the phone.

fill.q: 수박은 비싸지만 바나나___ 저렴해요.
fill.en: Watermelon is expensive, but bananas are inexpensive.

cards.en: I read a book. (object with final consonant)
I wash an apple. (object without final consonant)
I listen to music. (listening target)
I watch a movie. (watching target)
I do homework. (doing target)
I meet a friend. (meeting target)
I take a photo. (photographing target)
I learn Korean. (learning target)

quiz.q: Which sentence correctly uses the object marker 을/를?
quiz.why: 신문 ends with a final consonant (ㄴ), so it requires the object marker 을.

quiz.q: Which sentence has an INCORRECT object marker?
quiz.why: 창문 ends with a final consonant (ㄴ), so it must take 을 (창문을 열어요).

quiz.q: Which particle correctly completes: '부모님께 안부 전화___ 드렸어요'?
quiz.why: 전화 ends with a vowel, so the object marker 를 attaches to complete the object of 드렸어요.

quiz.q: Why is '빵을 먹어요' correct instead of '빵를 먹어요'?
opts: 빵 ends with a final consonant (ㅇ).
quiz.why: Because 빵 has a final consonant (받침 ㅇ), it takes 을 instead of 를.

quiz.q: Which sentence correctly marks the object in: 'I bought shoes yesterday'?
quiz.why: 신발 is the object of the transitive verb 샀어요 (bought), so it takes 을.

fill.q: 아침에 따뜻한 국___ 끓였어요.
fill.en: I boiled warm soup in the morning.

fill.q: 주말마다 도서관에서 소설책___ 빌려요.
fill.en: Every weekend, I borrow novel books from the library.

fill.q: 점심시간에 시원한 보리차___ 마셨어요.
fill.en: During lunchtime, I drank cool barley tea.

fill.q: 외출하기 전에 가방___ 챙겼어요.
fill.en: Before going out, I packed my bag.

fill.q: 식사 후에 달콤한 케이크___ 먹었어요.
fill.en: After the meal, I ate sweet cake.

cards.en: The teacher's book. (possession)
Mother's glasses. (possession)
Our dream. (collective possession)
Korea's culture. (characteristic / belonging)
My bag. (contracted from 나의)
My wallet (humble). (contracted from 저의)
Friend's birthday. (event belonging to friend)
Today's weather. (time attribute)

quiz.q: How is the possessive particle 의 usually pronounced in spoken Korean when marking possession?
quiz.why: In standard Korean phonology, the possessive particle 의 is commonly pronounced as [에] in everyday speech.

quiz.q: What is the contracted form of 저의 (my, humble)?
quiz.why: 저의 (humble my) contracts to 제, while 나의 (plain my) contracts to 내.

quiz.q: Which sentence correctly uses the possessive particle 의?
quiz.why: The particle 의 links the owner 민수씨 to the owned item 우산.

quiz.q: Which pair shows a contracted possessive pronoun correctly?
quiz.why: 나의 contracts to 내 (for example, 내 친구 means my friend).

quiz.q: Which phrase correctly means 'the future of our country'?
quiz.why: The particle 의 indicates belonging or connection, meaning of our country.

fill.q: 이것은 아버지___ 시계예요.
fill.en: This is father's watch.

fill.q: 저___ 취미는 여행 사진 촬영이에요.
fill.en: My hobby is travel photography.

fill.q: 그것은 우리 팀___ 공통 목표예요.
fill.en: That is our team's common goal.

fill.q: 민호___ 생일 파티에 초대받았어요.
fill.en: I was invited to Minho's birthday party.

fill.q: 도서관 입구에 오늘___ 추천 도서 목록이 붙어 있어요.
fill.en: Today's recommended book list is posted at the library entrance.

cards.en: There is a bed in the room. (static location)
There is no one at the company. (location of non-existence)
I live in Seoul. (residence location)
I wake up at seven o'clock. (specific time point)
There is an exam on Monday. (day of week)
I take a walk on the weekend. (time period)
Let us meet in the afternoon. (time of meeting)
A bird is sitting in the tree. (location where something rests)

quiz.q: Which word CANNOT take the time particle 에?
quiz.why: Relative time words like 오늘 (today), 어제 (yesterday), and 내일 (tomorrow) do not take the particle 에.

quiz.q: Which sentence correctly marks a location of existence with 있다?
quiz.why: With the verb 있다 (to exist), the static location where an item exists takes the particle 에, not 에서.

quiz.q: Which sentence has an INCORRECT use of 에?
quiz.why: 어제 is a relative time word and cannot be followed by 에 (say 어제 친구를 만났어요).

quiz.q: Fill in the blank: '저는 지금 서울___ 살고 있어요.'
quiz.why: The verb 살다 (to live) takes the location particle 에 to indicate one's place of residence.

quiz.q: What does 에 indicate in '기차가 다섯 시에 도착해요'?
quiz.why: Attached to 다섯 시 (5 o'clock), 에 indicates the specific time at which the action occurs.

fill.q: 냉장고___ 신선한 우유가 가득 들어 있어요.
fill.en: The refrigerator is full of fresh milk.

fill.q: 매일 아침 일곱 시 반___ 지하철을 타요.
fill.en: I take the subway at 7:30 every morning.

fill.q: 우리 가족은 제주도___ 살아요.
fill.en: Our family lives in Jeju Island.

fill.q: 이번 주 일요일___ 친구 결혼식이 있어요.
fill.en: There is a friend's wedding this Sunday.

fill.q: 교실 안 벽___ 세계 지도가 걸려 있어요.
fill.en: A world map is hanging on the wall inside the classroom.

cards.en: I go to school. (destination of movement)
I returned home. (destination of returning)
I arrived at the airport. (arrival destination)
I attend the gym regularly. (destination with 다니다)
How much is it per piece? (unit rate)
I take it three times a day. (frequency per time unit)
I exercise twice a week. (frequency per week)
It is 1,000 won per hour. (rate per hour)

quiz.q: Which sentence uses 에 to express a destination of movement?
quiz.why: In 도서관에 공부하러 가요, 에 marks 도서관 as the destination of the movement verb 가다.

quiz.q: What does 에 express in '사과가 한 개에 천 원이에요'?
quiz.why: When attached to counting classifiers like 한 개 (one piece), 에 means per or for each unit.

quiz.q: Which particle fits in: '이 약은 식후 삼십 분에 하루___ 세 번 드세요'?
quiz.why: 하루에 세 번 means three times a (per) day, expressing frequency per time unit.

quiz.q: Which verb commonly takes 에 to indicate the destination of moving toward?
quiz.why: Movement verbs like 가다 (to go) and 오다 (to come) take 에 to mark the destination.

quiz.q: Which sentence correctly expresses 'I go to the office by nine'?
quiz.why: 사무실에 출근해요 uses 에 to mark the office as the destination of going to work.

fill.q: 오후에 편지를 보내러 우체국___ 갔어요.
fill.en: In the afternoon, I went to the post office to send a letter.

fill.q: 이 귤은 한 상자___ 이만 원이에요.
fill.en: These tangerines are 20,000 won per box.

fill.q: 저는 한 달___ 한 권씩 책을 꼭 읽어요.
fill.en: I make sure to read one book per month.

fill.q: 비행기가 저녁 일곱 시에 인천공항___ 도착해요.
fill.en: The plane arrives at Incheon Airport at 7 PM.

fill.q: 퇴근길에 식료품을 사러 마트___ 들렀어요.
fill.en: On the way home from work, I stopped by the grocery mart.

cards.en: I eat a meal at the restaurant. (location of action)
I study for the exam at the library. (location of studying)
I jog in the park. (location of jogging)
I bought clothes at the department store. (location of purchase)
Where do you work? (location of work)
I came from the United States. (origin / starting point)
I get off at the station. (point of disembarking)
I rest at home. (location of resting)

quiz.q: What is the difference between 방에 and 방에서?
opts: 방에 is for action, 방에서 is for static existence.
방에 indicates existence or destination, while 방에서 marks the location of an active behavior.
방에 means from the room, 방에서 means toward the room.
There is no difference in usage.
quiz.why: 에 is used with verbs like 있다/없다/가다, whereas 에서 marks the dynamic place where an action takes place.

quiz.q: Which sentence correctly uses 에서 to indicate a place of action?
quiz.why: Drinking coffee is an active behavior taking place at the cafe, requiring the dynamic location marker 에서.

quiz.q: What does 에서 mean in '어느 나라에서 오셨어요?'?
quiz.why: With movement verbs like 오다 (to come), 에서 marks the starting point or place of origin (from).

quiz.q: Which sentence has an INCORRECT particle?
quiz.why: Watching a movie is an action taking place inside the cinema, so it must be 영화관에서, not 영화관에.

quiz.q: Which particle completes: '저는 어제 서점___ 소설책을 샀어요'?
quiz.why: Buying a book is an action performed at the bookstore, so 에서 is the correct marker.

fill.q: 주말에 근처 수영장___ 자유형을 연습했어요.
fill.en: Over the weekend, I practiced freestyle at the nearby swimming pool.

fill.q: 어느 나라___ 한국으로 오셨어요?
fill.en: From which country did you come to Korea?

fill.q: 점심시간에 구내식당___ 돈가스를 먹었어요.
fill.en: During lunchtime, I ate pork cutlet at the cafeteria.

fill.q: 동생은 자기 방___ 음악을 크게 듣고 있어요.
fill.en: My younger sibling is listening to music loudly in their room.

fill.q: 내일 오후에 중앙역 시계탑 앞___ 만나요.
fill.en: Let us meet in front of the Central Station clock tower tomorrow afternoon.

cards.en: From Seoul to Busan. (spatial range)
From home to the office. (spatial range)
From here to there. (spatial distance)
From 9 o'clock to 5 o'clock. (temporal range)
From Monday to Friday. (range of days)
From the beginning to the end. (range from start to finish)
From number 1 to number 10. (sequence range)
From yesterday to today. (calendar time range)

quiz.q: Which pair of particles is generally preferred for a starting and ending point in TIME?
quiz.why: For time periods (such as hours or days), 부터 - 까지 (from - until) is the standard pair.

quiz.q: Which pair of particles is generally preferred for a starting and ending point in PHYSICAL SPACE?
quiz.why: For physical locations and distances, 에서 - 까지 (from place to place) is used.

quiz.q: Which sentence has an INCORRECT particle combination?
quiz.why: For geographical locations, 에서 - 까지 is the standard (서울에서 부산까지), rather than 서울부터.

quiz.q: Fill in the blank: '점심시간은 열두 시___ 한 시까지예요.'
quiz.why: 열두 시 is a time point marking the beginning of an interval, so 부터 is appropriate.

quiz.q: Which particle fits in: '지하철역에서 우리 집___ 십 분 걸려요'?
quiz.why: 지하철역에서 marks the starting location, so 까지 marks the destination ending point.

fill.q: 기숙사에서 강의실___ 걸어서 십 분이면 가요.
fill.en: From the dormitory to the lecture room, it takes ten minutes on foot.

fill.q: 오전 아홉 시___ 오후 여섯 시까지 근무해요.
fill.en: I work from 9 AM to 6 PM.

fill.q: 제주공항___ 숙소까지 택시를 탔어요.
fill.en: I took a taxi from Jeju Airport to the lodging.

fill.q: 방학은 이번 주 금요일___ 시작해요.
fill.en: Vacation starts from this Friday.

fill.q: 선생님이 책 백 쪽부터 백오 쪽___ 풀라고 하셨어요.
fill.en: The teacher told us to solve from page 100 to page 105 of the book.

cards.en: I write a letter to a friend. (recipient of letter)
I gave a gift to my younger sibling. (colloquial recipient)
I inquired to the teacher. (honorific form of 에게/한테)
I give a snack to the puppy. (animal recipient)
To whom did you call? (colloquial phone recipient)
I sent regards to my parents. (honorific recipient)
I borrowed money from a friend. (source with 빌리다/받다)
I read a fairy tale book to children. (recipient of action)

quiz.q: What is the difference between 에게 and 한테?
opts: 에게 is for objects, while 한테 is for people.
에게 is commonly used in both writing and formal speech, while 한테 is more casual and conversational.
에게 is honorific, while 한테 is impolite.
There is no difference in tone or register.
quiz.why: Both attach to people or animals, but 에게 is standard/formal/written, whereas 한테 is informal and conversational.

quiz.q: Which particle is the HONORIFIC form of 에게/한테 used when directing an action to an elder?
quiz.why: 께 is the honorific dative particle used instead of 에게/한테 when giving something to an elder or respected person.

quiz.q: Can 에게/한테 attach to an inanimate building like 도서관?
opts: No, inanimate objects and locations take 에, not 에게/한테.
quiz.why: 에게/한테 is only used with people or animals. Inanimate objects and locations take the particle 에.

quiz.q: Which sentence correctly uses an honorific dative particle?
quiz.why: When offering something to grandparents (elders), the honorific particle 께 must be used with the verb 드리다.

quiz.q: Which particle completes: '짝꿍___ 연필 한 자루를 빌려주었어요'?
quiz.why: 짝꿍 (classmate) is a person receiving the lent item, so the dative particle 에게 (or 한테) is used.

fill.q: 생일을 맞은 친구___ 축하 카드를 보냈어요.
fill.en: I sent a congratulatory card to my friend celebrating a birthday.

fill.q: 배고픈 길고양이___ 사료를 챙겨 주었어요.
fill.en: I provided pet food to the hungry street cat.

fill.q: 조카___ 재미있는 장난감을 선물했어요.
fill.en: I gifted an interesting toy to my nephew.

fill.q: 할아버지___ 새해 안부 전화를 드렸어요.
fill.en: I made a New Year's greeting phone call to grandfather.

fill.q: 담임선생님___ 감사 편지를 정성껏 썼어요.
fill.en: I wrote a thank-you letter with all my heart to my homeroom teacher.

cards.en: Bread and milk. (과 with final consonant)
Apples and bananas. (와 without final consonant)
Rice and soup. (하고 used without form changes)
Pencil and notebook. (이랑 with final consonant)
I watch a movie with a friend. (companion with 랑)
I travel together with family. (formal companion with 과)
I talk with my older sister. (companion with 하고)
Spring and autumn. (connecting seasons)

quiz.q: Which pair of words correctly uses 와/과?
quiz.why: 선생님 ends with a final consonant (ㅁ), so it correctly takes 과, not 와.

quiz.q: Which connective particle has the SAME form regardless of whether the preceding noun has a final consonant?
quiz.why: 하고 attaches in the exact same form to both vowel-ending and consonant-ending nouns.

quiz.q: Which particle attaches correctly to 수박 (final consonant ㄱ) in casual spoken Korean?
quiz.why: Because 수박 ends with a final consonant (ㄱ), it takes 이랑 in colloquial spoken Korean.

quiz.q: Which sentence correctly expresses 'I went to the museum with my friend'?
quiz.why: 친구와 함께 means together with a friend, using the companion marker 와.

quiz.q: Which phrase has an INCORRECT particle choice?
quiz.why: 치마 ends in a vowel (마), so it must take 와 (치마와 바지), not 과.

fill.q: 아침 식사로 따뜻한 토스트___ 신선한 오렌지 주스를 먹었어요.
fill.en: For breakfast, I had warm toast and fresh orange juice.

fill.q: 문구점에서 필통___ 지우개를 새로 샀어요.
fill.en: At the stationery store, I bought a new pencil case and an eraser.

fill.q: 어제 방과 후에 친한 동기___ 같이 도서관에 갔어요.
fill.en: Yesterday after school, I went to the library together with a close classmate.

fill.q: 비빔밥에는 고추장___ 참기름이 꼭 들어가야 맛있어요.
fill.en: Red chili paste and sesame oil must go into bibimbap for it to taste delicious.

fill.q: 주말에 고향 친구___ 함께 한강 공원을 산책했어요.
fill.en: Over the weekend, I took a walk in Hangang Park together with a hometown friend.

cards.en: I am also a student. (replacing topic/subject)
I also bought apples. (replacing object)
I have also been to Korea. (adding to destination 에)
I also study at the library. (adding to dynamic location 에서)
I also sent it to a friend. (adding to recipient 에게)
It rains and the wind also blows. (parallel listing with 도)
There is not even one. (emphasis with negative verb)
I work even on weekends. (emphasis on time)

quiz.q: Which sentence correctly uses 도 to mean 'also' when replacing the object marker 을/를?
quiz.why: When attaching 도 to an object, it completely replaces 을/를, becoming 커피도 마셔요.

quiz.q: Can 도 attach after the location marker 에서?
quiz.why: Particles like 에서, 에, and 에게 can combine with 도, forming 에서도, 에도, and 에게도.

quiz.q: Fill in the blank: '지민 씨가 사과를 샀어요. 그리고 배___ 샀어요.'
quiz.why: Since Jimin bought apples and additionally bought pears, the addition marker 도 (also) is used.

quiz.q: What nuance does 도 express in '지갑에 동전이 하나도 없어요'?
opts: Strong emphasis meaning not even one
quiz.why: When combined with 하나 (one) and a negative predicate, 도 emphasizes not even one (none at all).

quiz.q: Which sentence has an INCORRECT combination with 도?
quiz.why: 도 replaces the subject/topic marker 은/는, so it must be 저도, not 저는도.

fill.q: 오늘 회의에 지수 씨___ 참석했어요.
fill.en: Jisu also attended today's meeting.

fill.q: 어제 피자를 먹고 파스타___ 먹었어요.
fill.en: Yesterday I ate pizza and also ate pasta.

fill.q: 우리 동네는 밤에___ 거리가 밝고 안전해요.
fill.en: In our neighborhood, the streets are bright and safe even at night.

fill.q: 냉장고 안에 물이 한 방울___ 남아 있지 않아요.
fill.en: Not even a single drop of water remains in the refrigerator.

fill.q: 도서관뿐만 아니라 집에서___ 열심히 복습해요.
fill.en: Not only at the library, but I also review diligently at home.

cards.en: I only drank water. (object exclusivity)
Only I did not know. (subject exclusivity)
I rest only on weekends. (time exclusivity with 에만)
I study only at home. (location exclusivity with 에서만)
Please wait just a moment. (quantity/time unit)
Please help me just once. (counting unit)
I only eat vegetables. (dietary exclusivity)
I told only my friend. (recipient exclusivity with 에게만)

quiz.q: Which sentence correctly expresses 'I only drank tea'?
quiz.why: When attached to a direct object, 만 replaces 을/를 completely to form 차만 마셨어요.

quiz.q: Can 만 attach after the particle 에서?
opts: Yes, it forms 에서만 meaning only at.
quiz.why: 만 can combine with prepositional particles like 에서 to form 에서만, meaning only at.

quiz.q: What does 만 express in '오 분만 쉬었다가 다시 시작합시다'?
quiz.why: Attached to 오 분 (five minutes), 만 limits the break to just or only five minutes.

quiz.q: Which sentence has an INCORRECT combination with 만?
quiz.why: The particle 만 replaces the object marker 을/를, so it should be 김밥만, not 김밥을만.

quiz.q: Fill in the blank: '모두 왔는데 민수___ 아직 안 왔어요.'
quiz.why: Everyone arrived except Minsu, so 만 (only) specifies that Minsu is the exclusive one who has not arrived.

fill.q: 저는 아침에 사과 반 쪽___ 간단하게 먹어요.
fill.en: In the morning, I only eat half an apple simply.

fill.q: 이 비밀은 우리 둘___ 알고 있기로 해요.
fill.en: Let us keep this secret known only between the two of us.

fill.q: 평일에는 바빠서 토요일에___ 영화를 봐요.
fill.en: Since I am busy on weekdays, I watch movies only on Saturdays.

fill.q: 어려운 질문이라 정답을 지우 씨___ 맞혔어요.
fill.en: Because it was a difficult question, only Jiu got the correct answer.

fill.q: 실내에서는 이 슬리퍼___ 신어야 해요.
fill.en: Indoors, you must only wear these slippers.

cards.en: I only have 1,000 won (nothing but). (insufficient money)
Only one is left. (disappointing small amount)
There is no one but you. (exclusivity / relying on someone)
I only know Korean (no other language). (limitation with 모르다)
I drink nothing but water. (exclusivity with negative verb)
I could only sleep for 30 minutes. (insufficient sleep)
Only three people came. (fewer attendees than expected)
There is no other way but this. (only remaining option)

quiz.q: What kind of verb MUST always follow the particle 밖에?
opts: A negative predicate (없다, 안, 못, etc.)
quiz.why: The particle 밖에 must always be paired with a negative predicate like 없다, 안, or 못.

quiz.q: Which sentence is grammatically INCORRECT because of the verb choice after 밖에?
quiz.why: The predicate after 밖에 must be negative. 하나밖에 있어요 is ungrammatical; it should be 하나밖에 없어요 or 하나만 있어요.

quiz.q: What nuance does 밖에 express compared to 만?
opts: A feeling that the quantity is smaller than expected or regrettable
quiz.why: While 만 simply states exclusivity, 밖에 highlights that the amount is small, insufficient, or regrettable.

quiz.q: Which sentence correctly expresses: 'I only slept two hours last night'?
quiz.why: The negative adverb 못 combines with 밖에 to express that sleeping two hours was insufficient.

quiz.q: Fill in the blank: '지갑에 버스비 오백 원___ 남아 있지 않아요.'
quiz.why: With the negative ending 남아 있지 않아요, 밖에 expresses that only 500 won remains.

fill.q: 주머니에 동전 몇 개___ 없어서 음료수를 못 샀어요.
fill.en: Because I had nothing but a few coins in my pocket, I could not buy a drink.

fill.q: 약속 시간까지 십 분___ 안 남았으니 서둘러요.
fill.en: There are only ten minutes left until the appointment time, so hurry.

fill.q: 교실에 학생이 두 사람___ 안 와서 쓸쓸해요.
fill.en: Only two students came to the classroom, so it feels lonely.

fill.q: 너무 피곤해서 어젯밤에 세 시간___ 못 잤어요.
fill.en: Because I was so tired, I could only sleep for three hours last night.

fill.q: 지금은 이 방법___ 다른 해결책이 전혀 없어요.
fill.en: Right now, there is no other solution at all but this method.

cards.en: Coffee or tea. (choice without final consonant)
Watermelon or strawberries. (choice with final consonant)
Saturday or Sunday. (choosing between days)
Mountains or the sea. (choice of destinations)
Shall we watch a movie or something? (suggesting an option)
Let us have tea or something. (casual suggestion)
Bread or rice. (food options)
Subway or bus. (transportation options)

quiz.q: Which pair of nouns correctly uses (이)나 to mean 'or'?
quiz.why: 주스 ends with a vowel, so it takes 나 (주스나 우유) instead of 이나.

quiz.q: Which noun requires 이나 because it ends with a final consonant?
quiz.why: 가방 ends with the final consonant (ㅇ), so it takes 이나 (가방이나 지갑).

quiz.q: What does 나 mean in '주말에 심심한데 영화나 볼까요?'?
opts: Suggesting an acceptable option (a movie or something)
quiz.why: (이)나 can be used to suggest an option casually, meaning something like or or something.

quiz.q: Which sentence has an INCORRECT form of (이)나?
quiz.why: 커피 ends in a vowel, so it must take 나 (커피나 녹차), not 커피이나.

quiz.q: Fill in the blank: '배가 고프니 라면___ 끓여 먹읍시다.'
quiz.why: 라면 ends with a final consonant (ㄴ), so the particle 이나 is used to suggest cooking ramen.

fill.q: 아침에 보통 빵___ 시리얼을 간단히 먹어요.
fill.en: In the morning, I usually eat bread or cereal simply.

fill.q: 피곤할 때는 따뜻한 녹차___ 유자차를 마셔요.
fill.en: When tired, I drink warm green tea or citron tea.

fill.q: 이번 휴가에는 부산___ 강릉으로 여행을 가고 싶어요.
fill.en: For this vacation, I want to travel to Busan or Gangneung.

fill.q: 주말에 시간이 나면 집에서 소설책___ 읽을 생각이에요.
fill.en: If I have time on the weekend, I plan to read a novel or something at home.

fill.q: 목이 많이 마른데 시원한 음료수___ 한 캔 사 마실까요?
fill.en: I am very thirsty; shall we buy and drink a cool soda or something?

cards.en: I waited as long as three hours! (unexpected long duration)
I drank as many as five cups! (large quantity of drinks)
As many as 100 people came! (large crowd)
I ate as many as five apples! (counter ending in vowel + 나)
I read as many as ten books! (large number of books)
It took as long as a whole month! (surprising duration)
It costs as much as 10,000 won! (surprising high price)
I called as many as ten times! (high frequency)

quiz.q: What nuance does (이)나 express in '어제 열 시간이나 잤어요'?
opts: Surprise at sleeping as long as ten hours
Choice between ten hours or more
quiz.why: Attached to a number or counter, (이)나 expresses surprise that the quantity or duration is larger than expected.

quiz.q: Which counter correctly takes 나 instead of 이나?
quiz.why: 개 ends in a vowel (ㅐ), so it attaches directly to 나 (세 개나), while 권, 명, and 시간 end in consonants.

quiz.q: Which sentence has an INCORRECT particle form?
quiz.why: 개 ends with a vowel, so it must take 나 (세 개나), not 세 개이나.

quiz.q: Fill in the blank: '비행기 표가 백만 원___ 해서 깜짝 놀랐어요.'
quiz.why: 원 ends with a final consonant (ㄴ), so 이나 is attached to express shock at the high price.

quiz.q: Which sentence expresses that eating three bowls of noodles was a surprisingly large amount?
quiz.why: 그릇 ends with a final consonant, so 이나 expresses that three bowls is a surprisingly large amount.

fill.q: 어제 시험공부를 하느라 새벽 세 시___ 깨어 있었어요.
fill.en: Studying for the exam yesterday, I was awake until as late as 3 AM.

fill.q: 콘서트 티켓을 사려고 줄을 두 시간___ 서 있었어요.
fill.en: To buy concert tickets, I stood in line for as long as two hours.

fill.q: 점심에 너무 배가 고파서 만두를 열 개___ 혼자 다 먹었어요.
fill.en: Because I was so hungry at lunch, I ate as many as ten dumplings all by myself.

fill.q: 그 축제에는 외국인 관광객이 천 명___ 모였어요.
fill.en: As many as 1,000 foreign tourists gathered at that festival.

fill.q: 기숙사 방 청소를 한 지 벌써 한 달___ 지났어요.
fill.en: As long as a whole month has already passed since I cleaned my dorm room.

cards.en: I write with a pencil. (tool ending in ㄹ -> 로)
I cut with scissors. (tool ending in vowel -> 로)
I eat with a spoon. (tool ending in consonant -> 으로)
I go by subway. (means of transportation)
Please go to the right. (direction)
Speak in Korean. (language/medium)
Tofu is made from soybeans. (raw material)
Depart toward Seoul Station. (direction of travel)

quiz.q: Which noun ending with a final consonant exceptionally takes 로 instead of 으로?
opts: Words ending in ㄹ (such as 연필, 칼, 서울)
quiz.why: Nouns ending in the final consonant ㄹ (like 연필, 칼, 서울) take 로 rather than 으로.

quiz.q: Which sentence correctly attaches (으)로 to express a tool?
quiz.why: 젓가락 ends with the final consonant ㄱ, so it takes 으로 (젓가락으로).

quiz.q: What does (으)로 indicate in '저 사거리에서 왼쪽으로 도세요'?
quiz.why: Attached to 왼쪽 (left), 으로 indicates the direction in which to turn.

quiz.q: Which phrase has an INCORRECT form of (으)로?
quiz.why: 비행기 ends with a vowel (기), so it must take 로 (비행기로), not 비행기으로.

quiz.q: Fill in the blank: '저는 부산까지 빠른 기차___ 이동했어요.'
quiz.why: 기차 ends in a vowel, so the particle 로 expresses the means of transportation.

fill.q: 상자를 튼튼한 테이프___ 꼼꼼하게 붙였어요.
fill.en: I taped the box meticulously with strong tape.

fill.q: 이 국물 요리는 숟가락___ 드시면 편리해요.
fill.en: It is convenient if you eat this soup dish with a spoon.

fill.q: 지하철 출구에서 나와서 오른쪽___ 오십 미터만 오세요.
fill.en: Come out of the subway exit and come just 50 meters to the right.

fill.q: 친구와 비밀 이야기를 한국어___ 나누었어요.
fill.en: I shared secret stories with my friend in Korean.

fill.q: 이 빵은 고소한 쌀가루___ 정성껏 만들었어요.
fill.en: This bread was made with all heart from flavorful rice flour.

cards.en: Let us meet around three o'clock. (approximate time)
It takes about thirty minutes. (estimated duration)
About ten people gathered. (estimated count)
It costs around 1,000 won. (estimated price)
I will depart around tomorrow. (estimated date)
I finished about half of it. (estimated portion)
About two kilometers remain. (estimated distance)
How many days will it take approximately? (inquiry of estimate)

quiz.q: What does the particle 쯤 mean when attached to a number or time?
quiz.why: 쯤 indicates an approximation, estimate, or rough guess (about, around).

quiz.q: Does the form of 쯤 change depending on whether the noun ends with a final consonant?
opts: Yes, it changes to 이쯤 after a consonant.
No, it is always 쯤 regardless of final consonants.
quiz.why: The particle 쯤 has a single fixed form and attaches directly to nouns whether they have a final consonant or not.

quiz.q: Which sentence correctly uses 쯤 to estimate time?
opts: 내일 오후 두 시쯤 커피숍에서 만나요.
내일 오후 두 시이쯤 커피숍에서 만나요.
내일 오후 두 시을쯤 커피숍에서 만나요.
내일 오후 두 시로쯤 커피숍에서 만나요.
quiz.why: 쯤 attaches directly to time nouns: 두 시쯤 means around 2 o'clock.

quiz.q: Which question asks for an approximate count using 쯤?
quiz.why: 몇 명쯤 means approximately how many people.

quiz.q: Fill in the blank: '역까지 걸어가면 십오 분___ 걸려요.'
quiz.why: 십오 분쯤 means about 15 minutes, expressing an estimated duration.

fill.q: 퇴근하고 집에 도착하면 저녁 일곱 시___ 될 거예요.
fill.en: When I arrive home after work, it will be around 7 PM.

fill.q: 오늘 동아리 모임에 스무 명___ 참석할 예정이에요.
fill.en: About twenty people are scheduled to attend today's club meeting.

fill.q: 학교 도서관까지 걸어서 십 분___ 걸려요.
fill.en: It takes about ten minutes on foot to the school library.

fill.q: 주문하신 음식은 십오 분___ 뒤에 나올 거예요.
fill.en: The food you ordered will come out in about 15 minutes.

fill.q: 이번 프로젝트는 다음 주 화요일___ 끝날 것 같아요.
fill.en: This project seems like it will finish around next Tuesday.

cards.en: Kind like an angel. (resemblance in personality)
Wide like the ocean. (resemblance in scale)
Beautiful like a movie. (resemblance in quality)
Drink it like water. (resemblance in manner)
Warm like family. (resemblance with 같이)
Pretty like a picture. (scenic beauty)
Disappeared like a lie. (figurative manner)
Act as usual. (comparison with standard/usual)

quiz.q: What do 처럼 and 같이 mean when attached to a noun in '천사처럼 웃어요'?
quiz.why: Attached to a noun, 처럼 or 같이 means like or as, drawing a comparison of resemblance.

quiz.q: Which sentence has the same meaning as '가족처럼 지내요'?
quiz.why: The particles 처럼 and 같이 are interchangeable when expressing resemblance (like family).

quiz.q: Does 처럼 change form based on the presence of a final consonant?
opts: No, it attaches directly as 처럼 to all nouns.
quiz.why: The particle 처럼 has an invariant form and attaches directly to any noun.

quiz.q: Which sentence correctly describes someone singing like a bird?
quiz.why: 새처럼 means like a bird, comparing the voice to a bird.

quiz.q: Fill in the blank: '창밖 풍경이 한 폭의 그림___ 아름다워요.'
quiz.why: 그림처럼 (or 그림같이) means like a painting, depicting poetic resemblance.

fill.q: 제 친구는 마음씨가 바다___ 넓고 따뜻해요.
fill.en: My friend's heart is wide and warm like the ocean.

fill.q: 선생님은 우리를 친자식___ 다정하게 챙겨 주셨어요.
fill.en: The teacher took care of us warmly like their own children.

fill.q: 봄비가 내리더니 거짓말___ 하늘이 다시 맑아졌어요.
fill.en: After the spring rain fell, the sky became clear again like magic.

fill.q: 오늘 아침에도 평소___ 일찍 일어나서 조깅을 했어요.
fill.en: This morning as well, I woke up early as usual and jogged.

fill.q: 그 가수는 밤하늘의 별___ 밝게 빛나는 목소리를 가졌어요.
fill.en: That singer has a voice that shines brightly like stars in the night sky.

cards.en: It is colder than yesterday. (comparison with time)
Airplanes are faster than trains. (comparison between transports)
Korean is more difficult than English. (comparison of difficulty)
The older brother is taller than the younger sibling. (comparison of height)
The movie is more interesting than the book. (comparison of interest)
It is easier than I thought. (comparison with expectation)
Action is more important than words. (comparison of importance)
Health is the best above anything else. (superlative comparison)

quiz.q: In the sentence '수박이 사과보다 커요', which fruit is bigger?
quiz.why: The particle 보다 attaches to the baseline of comparison (사과). So watermelon is bigger than apple.

quiz.q: Which word is often used alongside 보다 to emphasize 'more'?
quiz.why: 더 (more) commonly reinforces comparative statements using 보다 (for example, 어제보다 더 더워요).

quiz.q: Does 보다 change form when attached to a noun with a final consonant?
opts: No, it is always 보다 on all nouns.
quiz.why: The particle 보다 has a constant form and attaches directly to nouns with or without a final consonant.

quiz.q: Which sentence correctly expresses: 'Today is warmer than yesterday'?
quiz.why: 어제보다 attaches 보다 to yesterday as the point of comparison, meaning warmer than yesterday.

quiz.q: Fill in the blank: '이번 시험은 지난번 시험___ 훨씬 쉬웠어요.'
quiz.why: 보다 attaches to 지난번 시험 to mean much easier than the previous exam.

fill.q: 고속열차는 시외버스___ 속도가 훨씬 빨라요.
fill.en: The high-speed train is much faster in speed than the intercity bus.

fill.q: 오늘 낮 기온은 어제___ 삼 도 더 높아요.
fill.en: Today's daytime temperature is 3 degrees higher than yesterday.

fill.q: 직접 만들어 보니 생각___ 어렵지 않았어요.
fill.en: When I tried making it myself, it was not as difficult as I thought.

fill.q: 인생에서는 돈___ 건강이 훨씬 더 중요해요.
fill.en: In life, health is much more important than money.

fill.q: 이 전자사전은 종이책 사전___ 가볍고 편리해요.
fill.en: This electronic dictionary is lighter and more convenient than a paper book dictionary.

cards.en: I exercise every day. (daily recurrence)
I hike every weekend. (weekly recurrence)
I drink coffee every morning. (time interval recurrence)
Each person has different thoughts. (individual difference)
Every country has different culture. (cultural variation)
There is an air conditioner in every room. (spatial distribution)
The bus comes every ten minutes. (time frequency interval)
I go on a trip every year. (yearly recurrence)

quiz.q: What does 마다 mean in '아침마다 조깅을 해요'?
quiz.why: The particle 마다 indicates repetition without exception (every morning).

quiz.q: Does 마다 change form after a final consonant?
opts: No, it attaches directly as 마다 to all nouns.
quiz.why: The particle 마다 attaches directly to all nouns without form change.

quiz.q: Which sentence expresses: 'Every person has a different taste'?
quiz.why: 사람마다 means each and every person, expressing individual differences.

quiz.q: Fill in the blank: '지하철은 출근 시간에 삼 분___ 한 대씩 와요.'
quiz.why: 삼 분마다 means every three minutes, indicating regular time intervals.

quiz.q: Which phrase has an INCORRECT particle choice for 'every weekend'?
quiz.why: 마다 attaches directly without adding 이; 주말이마다 is ungrammatical.

fill.q: 저는 아침___ 따뜻한 보리차 한 잔을 마셔요.
fill.en: Every morning, I drink a cup of warm barley tea.

fill.q: 나라___ 전통 명절을 보내는 방식이 달라요.
fill.en: Every country has a different way of spending traditional holidays.

fill.q: 시내버스가 십 분___ 정류장에 도착해요.
fill.en: The city bus arrives at the stop every ten minutes.

fill.q: 계절___ 피어나는 꽃의 색깔과 향기가 달라요.
fill.en: The colors and scents of blooming flowers differ with each season.

fill.q: 우리 가족은 주말___ 근처 공원에서 함께 자전거를 타요.
fill.en: Every weekend, our family rides bicycles together in the nearby park.
